page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre; page number top right. Below: a title block "P. MELISSO SCHEDIO." with a poem of 10 lines in the main column; then a second title "IN PONTICVM." with a poem of 10 lines. Single column, no marginal notes. Catchword/signature at foot.

l.i: Elegantissime, quaso, mi Melisse, Quo mellita magis nec ipsa mella,
Ac ipsi lepidi magis lepores,
Ac est ipsa Venus magis Venusta,
Ipsnam hoc nomine te beauit augur?
Vllor, an tibi vel novem Camoenæ.
Ipsa Charites tibi hoc, Melisse,
Quasi puero dedere nomen?
Ô parcite vos mihi, Camoenæ,
Vos ô Charites. Melissus iste
Vorsum? Nam potius vel est melipsum,
Vt est ipsa opifex μελίσσα mellis,
Vt certe ipsius officina mellis.
Sse lupum nosti, pastoris nomine falso
Commissas tectus qui sibi glubit oues.
Vt tamen argentum, das aurum, prædia, villas,
Et quascunque lupi flagitat ingluuies.
Tm tibi religio est illum ablegare petentem,
Ast huic religio est maxima non capere. I-
gitur quiduis, & quiduis arripit ille:
Tu dando, hic nunquam est accipiendo satur.
Peccata, inquis, redimā. Immo quis furor hic
est, Vt pecudem ferues, pascere velle lupum?

page.notes: Printed text is partly damaged and italic; several words read with doubt (e.g., "Elegantissime", "quaso", "Camoenæ", "Charites", "melipsum", "Venusta" ). Lines at the foot of the page are cut off by the scan edge; the word "M" with a signature mark appears at the bottom and is the gathering signature, reading "M 2" approximately.
